value_or_angle: header="The first iron furnace in the West" body="L.B. came to Oregon in 1873, at twenty-two, to run the iron furnace at Oswego, the first west of the Mississippi. His syndicate raised its stone stack from thirty-two feet to forty-two and laid a narrow-gauge railroad to the Prosser mine." category=business

value_or_angle: header="Four steamers on Northwest rivers" body="With Captain U. B. Scott, an old Ironton friend of the family, and E. W. Crichton, who had learned the iron trade beside him, L.B. built and ran the steamers Ohio, Fleetwood, Telephone and Flyer." category=business

value_or_angle: header="A cane from Washington's tomb" body="About 1871 L.B. cut a small evergreen at George Washington's tomb at Mount Vernon and made a cane of it for his father, Boudinot. By 1926 it had passed to the fourth generation, his grandson Tyler Woodward Seeley." category=family

value_or_angle: header="At seventy-five, a poem for Oregon" body="On his seventy-fifth birthday in 1926 L.B. wrote a poem to Oregon and proposed that the old furnace stack at Oswego, forty-two feet of hewn stone, carry a statue of Sam Simpson, the poet of the Willamette." category=character

value_or_angle: header="Home to his father's farm in 1873" body="In 1873 Boudinot brought his family back to the Painesville farm his father Uriah had cleared in 1815, because Uriah was old and the children needed schooling. He farmed its three hundred acres until he moved to Oregon in 1893." category=family
